title: Progressive hypothesis-driven eval lab (scratchbook)
content:
Goal / why this exists:

- I want a lightweight, iterative playground for running small-scale evaluation hypotheses against live traffic samples and synthetic variants, without committing to a full-blown eval job in Evals. Focus is speed of iteration and hypothesis refinement.
- Use case: product or SRE folks want to test whether a sampling change (e.g., temperature, top-p) or small prompt tweak materially changes key metrics (latency, token cost, error rate, helpfulness proxy) for a targeted user cohort.

High-level concept:

- Progressive hypothesis-driven eval: define a hypothesis, choose cohorts, spin up an ephemeral runner that samples requests (or replays offline requests), runs N variants (control + k experiments), computes quick metrics and visual diffs, and surfaces obvious wins (or regressions).
- Keep everything ephemeral: results stored short-term in Console experiment view, with a link to promote to a persistent eval in Evals or a Canary rollout in Console.

Minimum viable flow (developer/product POV):

1) New experiment in the Playground UI or CLI.
   - Name: quick-ttl-tree-clarity-2026-03
   - Hypothesis textbox: "Lower temperature from 0.8 to 0.6 for transactional assistant reduces hallucination tokens by 15% without hurting task completion proxy"
   - Choose variant configs (JSON): control = {temp:0.8}, exp1 = {temp:0.6}, exp2 = {temp:0.5} (optional)
   - Cohort: live-sampled (1%) OR offline-upload (CSV of recent requests)
   - Duration/size: 5k requests OR 24h (whichever comes first)
   - Metrics: latency P95, token-per-response, failure rate, simple usefulness heuristic (presence of keywords / task-success regex), quality score via small LLM rubric (optional)

2) Runner executes: smart routing to appropriate model variant (same model, different sampling params) and logs minimal telemetry (token counts, latencies, and hashed prompt id).

3) Quick results page: side-by-side aggregations + sample pairs for manual review. Has flag buttons: promote-to-eval, promote-to-canary, archive.

User stories (examples):

- As a PM I want to quickly test whether reducing generation length cap on support replies keeps issues resolved while cutting cost.
- As an SRE I want to run a short experiment to see whether batching settings cause P95 regressions for small prompts.
- As a researcher I want to run a small rubric-based quality check across the top 50 representative queries to verify a quantization profile doesn't degrade helpfulness.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):

- UI/CLI to create a playable experiment with at least 2 variants and cohort selection.
- Runner that can operate in two modes: live-sample (via Console sampling hook / tracing toggle) and offline-replay (CSV upload of request payloads).
- Dashboard that shows aggregated metrics (mean tokens, token cost estimate, latency p50/p95, failure rate) and a side-by-side sample table.
- Link to promote experiment into existing Evals or to create a Console canary configuration.

Data & privacy notes:

- By default, sample only hashed user ids and hashed prompt ids in Playground logs; strip PII from stored samples.
- For offline uploads, warn user and require a checkbox confirming PII is removed.

Operational concerns / constraints:

- Must not degrade production latency; runner should route to compatible model variants and be rate-limited (e.g., at most 1% of production traffic unless an admin override).
- Experiment footprints should be capped (max N requests per experiment) and auto-stop when cap reached.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:

- Cohort selection UX: pre-built cohorts (top intents, edge cases, enterprise customers) vs free-form sampling filter (by route, by token distribution, by customer tag).
- Metric selection: do we surface a simple single-signal "quality delta" (composed metric) or leave it to users to pick multiple raw signals?
- How to ground quality checks: use a small in-house rubric LLM vs call out to user-provided check function? Costs for rubric LLM may be nontrivial.

Quick CLI prototype (notes):

- redwood eval-runner create "temp-check" --cohort "route:/support/reply" --sample 0.01 --variants '{"control":{"temp":0.8},"exp1":{"temp":0.6}}' --size 5000 --metrics "tokens,latency,fail_rate,heuristic_helpful"
- redwood eval-runner status <id>
- redwood eval-runner promote <id> --to canary | eval

Small UX sketch (Console):

- Left: experiment setup form; center: realtime status + aggregated numbers; right: sample viewer with tuneable sample filters (show only utterances where variants disagreed).
- CTA: "Promote to Canary" (creates canary configuration) and "Export as Evals" (creates YAML with sample and rubric to persist).

Risks / mitigation:

- Risk: Playground results could be misinterpreted (small N, noisy metrics).
  - Mitigation: big warning banner about statistical power, confidence intervals, and suggested minimum sizes.
- Risk: accidental exposure of PII.
  - Mitigation: auto-scrub patterns, require explicit consent for raw payload retention.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:

- Spike: implement a tiny runner that can replay a CSV of 500 items and compute tokens+latency (owner: Isha, 2d).
- Design: quick Console mockups for the experiment create flow (owner: Mika, 3d).
- Infra: draft rate-limiting and sampling hooks with SRE (owner: Ravi, sync this week).

Notes to self: keep scope narrow for MVP — aim for a tool that helps catch obvious regressions and gives product folks confidence to promote experiments to formal Evals or Canary rollouts.

Unfinished ideas / wishlist (low priority):

- Auto-suggest experimental variants based on past successful changes (e.g., suggest temp drop when hallucination rate > X).
- Cohort drift detector that alerts if the sampled cohort no longer matches historical distributions.
- Built-in A/B analytics integration (simple t-test / uplift estimator)

----

End of scratchbook.
